title: Platform scrum: rotations, fallback playbook, midweek notes
content:
Midweek platform scrum notes (Tuesday informal deep-dive)

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Arjun Singh, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Morris, Samira Alvarez, Joe Park (guest, SRE)

Purpose: reconcile oncall rotation confusion from last weekend, iterate fallback model for routing->auth->quota chain, and capture quick experiments to reduce latency regressions observed in Canary 14.

Agenda:
- Quick sync (5m)
- Root causes from weekend incident (15m)
- Fallback playbook audit + proposed edits (20m)
- Routing quota edge-case brainstorm + experiment plan (15m)
- Action items and owners (5m)

Notes / discussion highlights:
1) Weekend incident summary
- Context: 2026-06-05 02:12 UTC spike in auth token validation latency leading to cascading 503s on low-tier routes. Canary 14 saw increased p99 by ~420ms for auth calls; affected ~0.8% of requests overall.
- Immediate cause: short-lived Redis auth-cache evictions due to aggressive eviction policy during maintenance window; secondary cause: routing fallback incorrectly preferred model-variant that required KV-miss (extra DB lookup).
- Observation: Dedicated customers on route-level quotas experienced backpressure which surfaced as quota controller amplifying retries.
- Temporary mitigations: reverted cache TTL change, increased auth-service instance count for the window, turned on conservative routing-fallback to earlier stable variant.

2) Rotation / oncall friction points
- Pain: handoff notes from weekend shift lacked explicit TTL/config diffs. Current oncall template doesn't surface "recent config drifts" section.
- Proposal: add a one-page "config delta summary" to oncall handoff that includes last 72h of hot-config changes (links to PRs + envs). Maya to prototype template.
- Rota change suggestion: pair primary with a nominated "fallback owner" during maintenance windows to speed triage. Arjun to run a one-week trial.

3) Fallback playbook audit (routing -> auth -> quotas chain)
- We walked the playbook step-by-step and found two brittle checks:
  a) Routing decision logic that promoted model-variant B over baseline A when latency historical window < 200ms; this condition didn't consider increased KV miss rate.
  b) Quota controller fallback that retried on quota-deny with exponential backoff but no jitter, causing synchronized retries that doubled peak QPS.
- Edits proposed:
  * Add KV-miss rate to routing decision inputs (short window 30s).
  * Quota controller: change retry to randomized capped backoff (50-500ms) and short-term token-bucket smoothing when quota-deny detected across many routes.
  * Auth-service: fallback path should maintain an offline token validation cache (stale>fresh policy) for a short window to avoid DB calls on transient cache eviction.
- Impact verification: Priya will add these checks into the feature-flag rollout matrix and create unit tests for the randomized backoff.

4) Routing quota edge-cases + experiments
- Problem: low-tier routes (bursting background jobs) frequently trigger quota denials; controller treats denial as absolute until refill window. Some apps do safe retries which are fine; others retry aggressively.
- Experiment idea 1 (short-term): implement a soft-deny response (HTTP 429 with Retry-After computed by quota controller) for clients we control (internal keys). This gives client SDKs a chance to back off gracefully.
- Experiment idea 2 (mid-term): introduce adaptive refill where quota refill rate temporarily increases for routes with high success-to-failure ratio and low business-criticality. Needs SRE safety net.
- Data to collect: per-route retry pattern, success-after-retry ratio, per-customer customer-impact score. Ethan to pull initial 7-day data and produce a short dashboard widget in Console for test lanes.

5) Canary 14 latency regression triage
- Canary saw regressions mainly at sequence-length >1024 and with KV-cache miss path. Hypothesis: kernel selection path picks a slower matmul for certain sequence shapes under the new runtime optimizer.
- Action: create a micro-benchmark (arranged by Samira) that reproduces the sequence-length distribution; run between matmul kernels and capture raw timings. Samira to open a small perf PR and tag runtime team.

Decisions made:
- Adopt randomized capped backoff for quota retries (immediate).
- Add KV-miss as input to routing-fallback decision (spec by Priya).
- Oncall handoff template to include config-delta summary (prototype by Maya).

Action items (owner — due):
- Maya: prototype oncall "config delta" handoff template, post to Confluence for feedback — due 2026-06-10.
- Arjun: run 1-week trial of paired fallback owner during nightly maintenance windows and report findings — due 2026-06-14.
- Priya: update routing decision spec to include KV-miss metric and add unit tests + rollout flag — create PR INF-2413 — due 2026-06-11.
- Ethan: gather 7-day retry pattern data, produce Console widget mock, link to dashboard — due 2026-06-13.
- Samira: create micro-benchmark repo + perf PR for kernel selection repro, ping runtime team on Slack and put in weekly triage — due 2026-06-09.
- Joe Park (SRE): draft safety guardrail for adaptive refill experiment and validate resource impact using staging replay — due 2026-06-15.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we want soft-deny behavior for external customers or only internal clients initially? (Need product/CS input).
- What's the acceptable p99 delta for routing fallback experiments? Propose threshold = +10% absolute latency or 100ms whichever smaller. Need agreement from product.
- How to annotate rollback signals in the Console so operators can quickly see that a fallback is in effect (flag + timestamp)? Suggestion: add a per-route active fallback indicator; tracked as an event in traces.

War stories (short):
- Arjun recounted an incident where a misapplied rollout flag caused a model variant to be served to 20% of traffic but the fallout only showed for long-tail sequences; the lesson: tag rollout events with sequence-length distribution preview.

Notes to follow up in doc: link PRs and add timeline of last weekend incident once Arjun uploads logs (S3 path).

Quick wins suggested (low-effort):
- Add jitter to quota retry in controller (PR can be small).
- Add "recent config delta" section to existing oncall template page.

Meeting close: next check-in scheduled Thursday short sync (10m) to review PR statuses and Arjun's trial early signals.

Raw links referenced in meeting:
- INF-2413 (routing decision KV-miss flag)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/482 (recent quota-controller draft)
- Slack: #platform-ops (thread: PLAT-rotations-2026)

Document owner note: keep this file as the midweek working copy; we'll move finalized playbook edits into confluence:platform-rotations-playbook-2026 after PRs land.
